strengths: Novel application of prompt injection vulnerability for LLM provenance detection with clear motivation and intuitive connection
Comprehensive large-scale experimental evaluation on 5 base models with ~700 suspect models, achieving >90% TPR (gray-box) and >81% TPR (black-box) with near-zero FPR
Addresses practically important gray-box setting (token probability access) that was previously unexplored in LLM provenance literature
Sound technical approach with well-motivated loss functions (uniqueness + robustness), principled statistical threshold calibration, and extensive ablation studies

Strong robustness analysis including evaluation under prompt-injection detectors, adaptive attacks, scaling to larger models (14B), and insightful failure analysis showing misdetections correlate with model degradation
Practical consideration of real API constraints (e.g., top-k probabilities like ChatGPT), handling of both post-training and quantization post-processing
Well-written paper with clear presentation, comprehensive appendix with algorithmic details, and reproducible methodology
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: applies existing GCG algorithm without modifications and combines standard loss components; primary contribution is problem application rather than methodological innovation

Fundamental dependency on prompt injection vulnerability persisting in future models; limited discussion of degradation pathway as defenses improve, and vulnerability strength may vary significantly across architectures

Significant practical deployment barriers: fingerprint construction costs 60 GPU-hours; black-box verification requires ~30,000 queries (28 minutes); real-world APIs often have strict rate limits and query budgets

Threshold calibration depends on only 13 validation models with limited sensitivity analysis; empirical threshold selection presents as statistical guarantee but lacks formal rigor; unclear robustness to validation set selection or leakage

Limited generalization analysis: only recent open-source English models evaluated; no evaluation on older, closed-source, multilingual, very small, or domain-specific models; only first token considered
Complete evasion possible under white-box attack (Table 14, TPR=0) with potential gray-box evasion (83.3%); risk management strategy for fingerprint compromise inadequately addressed

Hyperparameter choices appear somewhat arbitrary despite ablations; semantic category-based token pairing not compared against alternatives; limited principled guidance for practitioners on new models
Limited analysis of why optimization beats heuristics; IPGuard comparison somewhat unfair due to adaptation from classifiers; LLMPrint-CA failure not thoroughly explained

Scope limitations: only first-token generation used without rigorous justification; unclear if multi-token sequences could provide stronger fingerprints; intra-family generalization (e.g., different Llama sizes) not explored
Missing code URL and incomplete reproducibility details; token pair independence and correlation properties not analyzed; theoretical lower bounds on robustness not discussed
